subject: Cross-dock maintenance window & rollback preflight for Private deployment
messages:
From: Tim Collins <tim.collins@acme-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2028-03-15T16:12:00Z
Subject: Private deployment preflight: cross-dock maintenance window proposal

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for taking time earlier. We're finalizing the maintenance window for our Private deployment (cross-dock VPC) and want to align on the upgrade plan, version pinning, and rollback expectations before we lock calendar invites. High-level ask from Acme: minimal downtime during daily ETL windows (02:00-04:00 UTC), a tested rollback path, and evidence of KV-cache compatibility when pinning to 1.7.x kernels.

Can your team confirm: 
- Recommended maintenance window(s) and how many stages (canary -> blue/green -> full cutover)?
- A short rollback checklist we can share with our on-call SREs (networking, routing, DNS, model pin fallback)?
- Any security attestations we need to hoist prior to starting (patch notes, CVE mitigations, SOC2 evidence)?

We can make the initial window the week of Mar 27 and would like an ops rehearsal the week prior if possible.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Collins
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Analytics
ops@acme-analytics.com

Attachment: none
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Collins <tim.collins@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T19:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight: cross-dock maintenance window proposal

Tim — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes we can support a staged canary -> staged rollout -> full cutover cadence with a rehearsal; we recommend a 3-stage window for this upgrade.

I'll loop in Irene for the network and rollback checklist. A couple of things we need from Acme before rehearsal:
- Confirmation of DNS TTLs for the inter-region endpoints (we prefer <= 60s for fast failover)
- A temporary ops escalation contact list with 24/7 reachable numbers
- Confirmation that you can accept brief read-only mode (30-90s) on the primary inference endpoint during swap — helps reduce KV-cache mismatch risk

Proposed dates: rehearsal — Mar 23 (US-friendly morning), maintenance window — Mar 28 02:00-06:00 UTC (canary 02:00-03:00, staged ramp 03:00-05:00, full cutover 05:00-06:00). If you want a smaller blast radius we can run an additional isolated canary on Mar 27.

I'll attach our preflight matrix and network diagram after Irene finalizes.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight: cross-dock maintenance window proposal

Folks — attaching the preflight matrix and an updated network diagram. Summary notes below; see matrix for step-by-step toggles.

Attachment stubs: preflight-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix with gating checks), network-diagram_v2.png (overlay of cross-dock peering & failover paths)

Key technical constraints and recommended gating checks:
1) Version pinning: if Acme requests pin to runtime 1.7.x we will: 
   - Publish a pinned config and a separate fallback config (1.6.x) with identical routing rules.
   - Create immutable canary group (5% traffic) with KV-cache warmup TTL of 600s prior to cutover.
2) Networking: 
   - Ensure health-check endpoints are reachable from both cross-dock peers over TLS 1.2+.
   - DNS TTLs <= 60s recommended; if you can only do 300s we will plan a longer soak period and staggered rollout.
3) Rollback checklist (high level):
   - Step 1: Pause new traffic to canary (via load balancer rule) and divert to fallback node group.
   - Step 2: Revert pinned config to 1.6.x in control plane (automated script, 2-step confirmation).
   - Step 3: Validate model inference sanity on fallback nodes (smoke tests + sample prompt set).
   - Step 4: Re-issue DNS/route changes if any, and reduce KV-cache TTL to enable fresh cache population.
4) Auditing: we'll snapshot audit logs (control plane + network) before and after cutover — provide hashes for your compliance team.

Open questions for Acme:
- Do you want Redwood to perform a brief read-only canary traffic run for 30 minutes after canary warmup, or would you prefer immediate policy-based ramping?
- Who is your on-call for Mar 23 rehearsal (name/phone)?

I'll be available for a quick runthrough tomorrow at 11:00 PT if that helps.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — that matrix looks good. A couple clarifying items from our side before rehearsal: 
- We prefer the read-only canary run for 30 minutes post-warmup to verify model outputs against baseline.
- Our DNS TTL is 120s (we can temporarily shorten to 60s for the window if necessary).
- On-call for workshop: Sarah Munroe (sarah.munroe@acme-analytics.com, +1-415-555-0132).

One ask: can you add a short subsection to the preflight matrix that covers the expected impact on telemetry (metric spike guidance, which traces we should watch for cache-miss storms)? Our compliance team wants concrete monitoring thresholds to sign off.

Also, would Redwood be able to produce a signed snapshot of the pre-cutover audit logs after rehearsal? That would speed up our internal approval.

—Tim

Tim — appreciated, that all works. Action items and next steps: 

1) Irene: add telemetry thresholds and a short monitoring runbook row to the preflight matrix (metric spike guidance, trace keys: /inference/latency, /cache/hits, /kv/miss-rate). Target: alert if latency > 150ms p95 or kv/miss-rate > 8%.
2) Acme: shorten DNS TTL to 60s for the rehearsal window (Mar 23) if possible; Sarah Munroe will be primary on-call.
3) Markus: I'll create the rehearsal calendar invite and Jira ticket INF-4762 (practice run checklist) and attach the updated matrix.
4) Compliance: Redwood will snapshot control-plane audit logs pre- and post-rehearsal and deliver signed hashes via DocuSign link in related_links.

Proposed rehearsal timeline (Mar 23):
- 10:00 PT: kickoff + runbook readout
- 10:20 PT: canary warmup (read-only 30m)
- 10:50 PT: validation and smoke tests
- 11:10 PT: staged ramp to 25% 
- 11:40 PT: rollback test (test revert to 1.6.x config)
- 12:00 PT: debrief

I'll create the invite for 10:00 PT and include the runbook. If anyone has objections to the thresholds above, flag now.

—Markus
Director, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
